# Images we are EVALUATING for the DHI mirror but have not adopted.
#
# Read by .github/workflows/dhi-list-tags.yml alongside the mirror list, so the
# tags dhi.io actually publishes for a candidate can be checked before anyone
# commits to a version. dhi.io refuses anonymous access, so this cannot be
# answered from a laptop — hence a workflow.
#
# Names only, no tags — the point is to discover what tags exist.
# Nothing here is mirrored or deployed. Move a line to dhi-mirror-images.txt
# (with a tag) to adopt it.

# Kong. The gateway is likely available; the ingress controller is the open
# question, and without it the pair splits across two provenance chains. Both
# upstream images are actively maintained and currently fresh (built within the
# last three weeks), so this is a consistency question, not a security one.
kong
kong-ingress-controller
kubernetes-ingress-controller

# The keycloak chart's realm-renderer and kc-init containers. They `apk add` at
# runtime, so a hardened runtime variant cannot work as a drop-in — probing to
# see what base variants exist for a purpose-built replacement image.
alpine

# ── Specific tags to inspect ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Written as name:tag, these get their entrypoint/cmd/user printed as well —
# what decides whether a variant can drop into a chart that starts its
# container with a shell.
kong:3.9.3

# ── Keycloak ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# RESOLVED, adopted: dockerfiles/keycloak/Dockerfile is FROM dhi.io/keycloak
# (build-keycloak-image.yml). The open question this block used to record —
# whether it could work at all, since our old ENTRYPOINT was the shell script
# /opt/keycloak/bin/kc.sh — is answered: DHI's own keycloak image ships kc.sh
# as ITS entrypoint too, i.e. it ships a shell by necessity. Booted against a
# real Postgres with both authenticator provider ids the shared realm's
# browser flows bind to registered.
